corpus_callosum: Anatomy - Large transverse nerve tract connecting the left and right cerebral hemispheres; agenesis presents with apraxia and interhemispheric disconnect.
internal_acoustic_meatus: Anatomy - Bony canal in the petrous temporal bone transmitting CN VII (facial) and CN VIII (vestibulocochlear) along with labyrinthine artery.
jugular_foramen: Anatomy - Skull base aperture transmitting CN IX, X, XI, and the internal jugular vein; glomus jugulare tumors arise here.
foramen_ovale: Anatomy - Sphenoid bone opening transmitting mandibular branch of trigeminal nerve (V3), accessory meningeal artery, and lesser petrosal nerve.
foramen_rotundum: Anatomy - Sphenoid bone passageway transmitting the maxillary nerve (V2) from middle cranial fossa to pterygopalatine fossa.
nucleus_solitarius: Anatomy/Physiology - Medullary visceral sensory nucleus receiving taste input (CN VII, IX) and visceral autonomic feedback (CN IX, X).
nucleus_dorsalis_of_clarke: Histology/Anatomy - Spinal cord gray matter column (T1-L2) giving rise to the dorsal spinocerebellar tract carrying unconscious proprioception.
red_nucleus: Anatomy/Physiology - Midbrain tegmental structure originating the rubrospinal tract, involved in motor coordination of upper limb flexors.
dentate_nucleus: Anatomy/Physiology - Largest and most lateral deep cerebellar nucleus; projects to contralateral VA/VL thalamus to plan voluntary movements.
hippocampus: Anatomy/Histology - Limbic structure in temporal lobe composed of dentate gyrus and CA fields; vital for consolidation of explicit long-term memory.
amygdala: Anatomy/Physiology - Temporal lobe limbic nucleus regulating emotional processing, fear conditioning, and autonomic stress responses.
clipping_of_aneurysm: Pathology/Surgery - Surgical placement of a metallic clip across the neck of a berry aneurysm to prevent subarachnoid hemorrhage rebleeding.
epidural_hematoma: Pathology - Skull fracture tearing middle meningeal artery; arterial blood collects between dura and skull; biconvex hyperdense lens shape on CT.
subdural_hematoma: Pathology - Tear of bridging veins causing crescent-shaped venous blood collection between dura and arachnoid; common in elderly and alcoholics.
subarachnoid_hemorrhage: Pathology - Rupture of saccular aneurysm causing blood accumulation in subarachnoid space; presents with thunderclap headache and xanthochromia.
intracerebral_hemorrhage: Pathology - Parenchymal brain bleeding most commonly caused by chronic hypertension leading to Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms in basal ganglia.
central_pontine_myelinolysis: A severe neurological condition characterized by iatrogenic loss of myelin sheaths in the pons, most commonly caused by overly rapid intravenous correction of chronic hyponatremia.
progressive_multifocal_leukoencephalopat: Pathology/Microbiology - Reactivation of JC virus in oligodendrocytes of immunocompromised patients; causes patchy multifocal CNS demyelination.
subacute_sclerosing_panencephalitis: Pathology/Microbiology - Late progressive fatal neurological complication occurring years after primary measles (rubeola) virus infection.
sydenham_chorea: Pathology/Microbiology - Autoimmune movement disorder following Streptococcus pyogenes pharyngitis; targeted anti-basal ganglia antibodies.
clostridium_botulinum: Microbiology - Anaerobic Gram-positive spore-forming rod producing botulinum toxin that cleaves SNARE proteins, blocking acetylcholine release.
clostridium_tetani: Microbiology - Anaerobic drumstick-shaped Gram-positive rod producing tetanospasmin toxin, blocking glycine/GABA release from Renshaw cells.
poliovirus: Microbiology - Picornavirus (+)ssRNA destroying anterior horn cells of spinal cord, resulting in asymmetric flaccid paralysis and muscle atrophy.
herpes_simplex_encephalitis: Microbiology/Pathology - HSV-1 reactivation causing hemorrhagic necrotizing encephalitis localized to the temporal lobes; CSF shows red blood cells.
epilepsy_absence: Pathology/Physiology - Generalized seizure characterized by 3 Hz spike-and-wave EEG pattern and brief consciousness loss; treated with ethosuximide.
ethosuximide: Pharmacology - Antiepileptic drug blocking T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons; first-line treatment for childhood absence seizures.
phenobarbital: Pharmacology - Barbiturate enhancing GABA-A receptor activity by increasing channel open duration; used for neonatal seizures.
diazepam: Pharmacology - Benzodiazepine binding GABA-A receptors to increase chloride channel opening frequency; acute treatment for status epilepticus.
levetiracetam: Pharmacology - Antiepileptic binding SV2A synaptic vesicle protein to inhibit neurotransmitter release; minimal CYP P450 interactions.
lamotrigine: Pharmacology - Antiepileptic blocking voltage-gated sodium channels and glutamate release; black box warning for Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
paranasal_sinuses: Anatomy - Air-filled ethmoid, frontal, maxillary, and sphenoid cavities lined by respiratory epithelium draining into nasal meatuses.
nasopharynx: Anatomy - Upper pharyngeal region posterior to nasal cavity containing pharyngeal tonsil (adenoid) and Eustachian tube openings.
vocal_cords: Anatomy/Histology - True vocal folds lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium to withstand mechanical stress during phonation.
bronchial_arteries: Anatomy - Branches of descending thoracic aorta providing oxygenated systemic blood supply to lung parenchyma and bronchial walls.
pulmonary_arteries: Anatomy/Physiology - Deoxygenated blood vessels originating from right ventricle carrying blood to pulmonary capillary bed for gas exchange.
trachealis_muscle: Anatomy/Histology - Smooth muscle band spanning the posterior open ends of C-shaped tracheal cartilages; constricts during coughing.
club_cells: Histology - Secretory non-ciliated cells in terminal bronchioles producing uteroglobin/CC16 and detoxifying agents via cytochrome P450.
goblet_cells: Histology - Mucus-secreting epithelial cells abundant in upper respiratory tract; decrease in number toward terminal bronchioles.
pulmonary_surfactant_proteins: Physiology - SP-A, SP-B, SP-C, SP-D proteins organizing dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine and promoting host defense against pathogens.
pulmonary_capillary_wedge_pressure: Physiology - Clinical measurement of left atrial pressure via Swan-Ganz pulmonary artery catheterization; elevated in cardiogenic edema.
anatomic_shunt: Physiology - Passage of blood from right to left heart without pulmonary gas exchange (e.g., bronchial veins draining into pulmonary veins).
bronchial_asthma_extrinsic: Pathology - IgE-mediated Type I hypersensitivity triggered by environmental allergens; characterized by eosinophilic pulmonary infiltration.
bronchiectatic_amyloidosis: Pathology - Secondary AA amyloid deposition in systemic tissues resulting from chronic suppurative lung infections like bronchiectasis.
silicosis: Pathology - Pneumoconiosis from inhaled silica dust causing nodular fibrotic lesions in upper lung lobes and eggshell calcification of hilar lymph nodes.
coal_workers_pneumoconiosis: Pathology - Inhalation of carbon particles causing anthracosis and hyperinflated emphysematous macules; can progress to progressive massive fibrosis.
berylliosis: Pathology - Metal exposure pneumoconiosis causing non-caseating granulomas in lungs and hilar lymph nodes, mimicking sarcoidosis.
haemophilus_influenzae_b: Microbiology - Encapsulated Coccobacillus causing acute epiglottitis ('thumbprint sign' on X-ray) and pediatric otitis media.
moraxella_catarrhalis: Microbiology - Gram-negative diplococcus causing respiratory tract infections, exacerbations of COPD, and acute sinusitis.
bordetella_pertussis: Microbiology - Gram-negative coccobacillus producing pertussis toxin (ADP-ribosylation of Gi); causes whooping cough with paroxysmal inspiratory whoop.
coxiella_burnetii: Microbiology - Obligate intracellular bacterium causing Q fever pneumonia and endocarditis; transmitted via farm animal spore inhalation.
montelukast_mechanism: Pharmacology - Selective leukotriene receptor antagonist blocking CysLT1 receptors; effective in preventing exercise-induced bronchospasm.
zileuton: Pharmacology - 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor preventing leukotriene B4, C4, D4, and E4 synthesis; requires monitoring of liver function tests.
omalizumab: Pharmacology - Monoclonal antibody binding free serum IgE, preventing binding to Fc-epsilon-R1 on mast cells; used in refractory asthma.
indacaterol: Pharmacology - Ultra-long-acting beta-2 agonist (Ultra-LABA) providing 24-hour bronchodilator coverage for maintenance COPD treatment.
roflumilast: Pharmacology - Oral phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE-4) inhibitor decreasing inflammation and airway smooth muscle remodeling in severe COPD.
renal_pyramid: Anatomy - Cone-shaped medullary structures containing parallel renal tubules and collecting ducts terminating at the renal papilla.
major_calyx: Anatomy - Large urine collection channel formed by convergence of several minor calyces, emptying into the renal pelvis.
detrusor_muscle: Anatomy/Physiology - Smooth muscle coat of urinary bladder wall contracts via parasympathetic stimulation (M3 receptors) during micturition.
internal_urethral_sphincter: Anatomy/Physiology - Involuntary smooth muscle sphincter at bladder neck controlled by sympathetic nerve fibers (alpha-1 receptors).
external_urethral_sphincter: Anatomy/Physiology - Voluntary skeletal muscle sphincter innervated by pudendal nerve (S2-S4) allowing voluntary urinary control.
podocyte_slit_diaphragm: A specialized cell junction between podocyte foot processes containing nephrin and podocin that acts as the final size- and charge-selective barrier preventing albuminuria.
extraglomerular_mesangium: Histology/Physiology - Cellular network between afferent/efferent arterioles and macula densa regulating autoregulatory vascular responses.
tubular_maximum_glucose: Physiology - Maximum reabsorptive rate of glucose in PCT (~375 mg/min); exceeding this threshold leads to glucosuria.
fractional_excretion_of_sodium: The percentage of sodium filtered by the glomeruli that is excreted in the urine (FENa), used to differentiate prerenal azotemia (<1%) from intrinsic acute tubular necrosis (>2%).
countercurrent_exchange: Physiology - Passive exchange of solutes and water between parallel ascending and descending vasa recta preserving medullary osmotic gradient.
urea_recycling: Physiology - Passive movement of urea from inner medullary collecting duct into interstitium mediated by ADH; contributes to hypertonicity.
renal_tubular_acidosis_type_1: Distal RTA characterized by an inability of alpha-intercalated cells to secrete H+, resulting in urine pH >5.5, hypokalemia, metabolic acidosis, and high risk of calcium phosphate nephrolithiasis.
renal_tubular_acidosis_type_2: Proximal RTA characterized by impaired HCO3- reabsorption in the proximal tubule, leading to urine pH <5.5 once systemic HCO3- drops below threshold, associated with Fanconi syndrome.
renal_tubular_acidosis_type_4: Hyperkalemic RTA caused by hypoaldosteronism or aldosterone resistance, leading to impaired ammonium (NH4+) excretion in the collecting duct and metabolic acidosis.
membranoproliferative_glomerulonephritis: Pathology - Immune complex disease with subendothelial deposits and C3 staining; light microscopy shows 'double-contour' tram-track GBM.
Pathology - Dense deposit disease caused by C3 nephritic factor stabilization of C3 convertase; intramembranous dense deposits.
rapidly_progressive_gn_type_2: Pathology - Immune-complex RPGN resulting from severe post-streptococcal GN, SLE nephropathy, or IgA nephropathy.
granulomatosis_with_polyangiitis: An ANCA-associated necrotizing vasculitis (PR3-ANCA / c-ANCA positive) affecting small vessels, characteristically involving the upper respiratory tract, lungs (cavitary lesions), and kidneys (crescents).
microscopic_polyangiitis: Pathology - MPO-ANCA/p-ANCA positive necrotizing vasculitis without granulomas; causes pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis.
churg_strauss_syndrome: Pathology - MPO-ANCA positive necrotizing vasculitis with eosinophilia, asthma, and necrotizing granulomas damaging renal glomeruli.
schistosoma_haematobium: Microbiology/Pathology - Trematode parasite with terminal spine eggs causing urinary schistosomiasis, hematuria, and squamous cell bladder cancer.
bk_virus_nephropathy: Microbiology/Pathology - Polyomavirus reactivation in renal transplant patients causing tubulointerstitial nephritis and viral inclusion intranuclear bodies.
bumetanide: Pharmacology - Potent loop diuretic inhibiting NKCC2 symporter in thick ascending limb; alternative for patients with furosemide resistance.
torsemide: Pharmacology - Long-acting loop diuretic inhibiting $Na^+/K^+/2Cl^-$ cotransporters; higher oral bioavailability than furosemide.
chlorthalidone: Pharmacology - Thiazide-like diuretic with long half-life inhibiting Na+/Cl- cotransporter in DCT; superior 24-hr BP reduction.
eplerenone: Pharmacology - Selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist blocking aldosterone without anti-androgenic side effects (no gynecomastia).
conivaptan: Pharmacology - Dual vasopressin V1A and V2 receptor antagonist used IV for acute euvolemic or hypervolemic hyponatremia.
tolvaptan: Pharmacology - Oral selective vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist used to slow kidney volume growth in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
chorda_tympani: Anatomy - Branch of CN VII that carries taste fibers from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and parasympathetic fibers to submandibular/sublingual glands.
foramen_spinosum: Anatomy - Skull base opening transmitting the middle meningeal artery and meningeal branch of CN V3.
superior_orbital_fissure: Anatomy - Sphenoid cleft transmitting CN III, IV, V1, VI, and ophthalmic veins into the orbit.
hypoglossal_canal: Anatomy - Occipital bone canal transmitting CN XII; lesions cause ipsilateral tongue deviation upon protrusion.
striatum_ventral: Anatomy/Physiology - Region including the nucleus accumbens, essential for reward processing, addiction, and dopaminergic signaling from VTA.
locus_coeruleus: Anatomy/Physiology - Noradrenergic nucleus in the posterior pons involved in arousal, stress response, and selective attention.
raphe_nuclei: Anatomy/Physiology - Serotonergic brainstem nuclei projecting widely throughout the CNS to modulate mood, sleep, and pain transmission.
substantia_nigra_pars_compacta: Anatomy/Physiology - Midbrain dopaminergic region projecting to the striatum; degeneration leads to motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease.
cerebellar_vermis: Anatomy/Physiology - Midline structure of the cerebellum regulating axial trunk stability, posture, and gait balance.
flocculonodular_lobe: Anatomy/Physiology - Vestibulocerebellum region controlling eye movements and balance via vestibular connections.
wallenberg_syndrome: Pathology - Lateral medullary infarction from PICA occlusion; causes loss of pain/temp on ipsilateral face and contralateral body, dysphagia, and Horner's syndrome.
weber_syndrome: Pathology - Midbrain stroke due to PCA occlusion affecting corticospinal tract and CN III; leads to ipsilateral oculomotor palsy and contralateral hemiparesis.
locked_in_syndrome: Pathology - Basilar artery occlusion resulting in ventral pontine infarction; spares vertical eye movements and consciousness while paralyzing all voluntary body movements.
charcot_bouchard_aneurysm: Pathology - Microaneurysm formation in small penetrating lenticulostriate arteries secondary to chronic hypertension; common cause of basal ganglia hemorrhage.
saccular_berry_aneurysm: Pathology - Outpouching at arterial branch points in the Circle of Willis (most commonly anterior communicating artery); rupture causes subarachnoid hemorrhage.
normal_pressure_hydrocephalus: Pathology - Triad of gait ataxia, urinary incontinence, and dementia ('wet, wacky, wobbly') caused by impaired CSF reabsorption; ventricles expand with normal pressure.
pseudotumor_cerebri: Pathology - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension in young obese females; causes severe headache, papilledema, and elevated opening pressure on lumbar puncture.
multiple_sclerosis: Pathology - Autoimmune demyelinating disorder of the CNS marked by oligodendrocyte loss, CSF oligoclonal bands, and relapsing-remitting optic neuritis or paralysis.
amyotrophic_lateral_sclerosis: A fatal neurodegenerative disease targeting both upper motor neurons in the cortex and lower motor neurons in the brainstem and spinal cord, causing progressive muscle atrophy, spasticity, and paralysis.
spinal_muscular_atrophy: Pathology - Autosomal recessive SMN1 gene mutation causing anterior horn cell degeneration; SMN protein deficiency leads to symmetrical proximal motor weakness in infants.
neisseria_meningitidis: Microbiology - Gram-negative diplococcus with polysaccharide capsule; major cause of epidemic bacterial meningitis in young adults; leads to Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome.
streptococcus_pneumoniae_cns: Microbiology - Lancets-shaped Gram-positive diplococcus; most common cause of community-acquired bacterial meningitis in adults.
cryptococcus_neoformans: Microbiology - Encapsulated yeast with narrow-based budding found in pigeon droppings; causes meningitis in AIDS patients; visualized with Mucicarmine or India ink.
cytomegalovirus_cns: Microbiology - Herpesvirus causing congenital periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, and chorioretinitis in newborns or encephalitis in immunocompromised patients.
ethosuximide_toxicity: Pharmacology - Adverse effects including gastrointestinal distress, lethargy, headache, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and blood dyscrasias.
primidone: Pharmacology - Antiepileptic metabolized to phenobarbital and phenylethylmalonamide; effective in managing essential tremor and focal seizures.
topiramate: Pharmacology - Broad-spectrum antiepileptic blocking sodium channels, enhancing GABA, and antagonizing AMPA receptors; side effects include weight loss and nephrolithiasis.
gabapentin: Pharmacology - Inhibitor of presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels ($N-type$) carrying alpha-2-delta subunit; used for neuropathic pain and focal seizures.
pregabalin: Pharmacology - High-affinity ligand to alpha-2-delta auxiliary subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels; used for postherpetic neuralgia and fibromyalgia.
perampanel: Pharmacology - Non-competitive AMPA glutamate receptor antagonist used as adjunctive therapy for focal and generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
nasal_septum: Anatomy - Osteochondral partition dividing the nasal cavity, formed by the perpendicular plate of ethmoid, vomer, and septal cartilage.
pyriform_aperture: Anatomy - Anterior bony opening of the nasal cavity bounded by nasal bones and maxillae.
maxillary_sinus: Anatomy - Largest paranasal sinus located within the maxilla; drains into the middle meatus via the hiatus semilunaris; highest risk of ostial obstruction.
type_1_pneumocyte: Histology - Thin squamous alveolar cell covering ~95% of alveolar surface area; optimized for gas diffusion.
type_2_pneumocyte: Histology - Cuboidal cell that synthesizes pulmonary surfactant (dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine) and serves as progenitor cell for repair after alveolar injury.
pulmonary_compliance: Physiology - Change in lung volume per unit change in transpulmonary pressure ($C = \\Delta V / \\Delta P$); decreased in pulmonary fibrosis, increased in emphysema.
airway_resistance: Physiology - Opposition to airflow through respiratory passages, governed by Poiseuille's law ($R \\propto 1 / r^4$); maximal in medium-sized bronchi.
ventilation_perfusion_ratio: Physiology - Ratio of alveolar ventilation to pulmonary capillary blood flow ($V/Q$); ideal ratio ~0.8; approaches infinity in dead space and zero in shunt.
alveolar_arterial_gradient: Physiology - Difference between alveolar and arterial oxygen tension ($A-a\\text{ gradient} = PAO_2 - PaO_2$); elevated in diffusion defects, $V/Q$ mismatch, and shunt.
carboxyhemoglobin: Physiology/Pathology - Form of hemoglobin bound to carbon monoxide; causes leftward shift of oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve and cellular hypoxia.
methemoglobinemia: Physiology/Pathology - Oxidation of iron in hemoglobin from ferrous ($Fe^{2+}$) to ferric ($Fe^{3+}$) state; leads to cyanosis and chocolate-colored blood.
chronic_bronchitis: Pathology - Productive cough for at least 3 consecutive months in 2 consecutive years; histologically defined by Reid index $> 50\\%$ hypertrophy of mucous glands.
emphysema_panacinar: Pathology - Destruction of entire acinus uniform in lower lobes; strongly associated with homozygous alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency ($PiZZ$).
emphysema_centrilobular: Pathology - Destruction of central proximal respiratory bronchioles with relative distal sparing; predominantly affects upper lobes in heavy smokers.
idiopathic_pulmonary_fibrosis: Pathology - Chronic progressive interstitial lung disease characterized by subpleural bibasilar honeycombing and usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) histology.
hypersensitivity_pneumonitis: Pathology - Immune-mediated granulomatous interstitial reaction to inhaled organic antigens (e.g., Farmer's lung); spares lung bases.
mycoplasma_pneumoniae: Microbiology - Cell-wall-deficient bacterium causing atypical 'walking' pneumonia; presents with high cold agglutinin titers (IgM).
chlamydia_pneumoniae: Microbiology - Obligate intracellular bacterium presenting with gradual onset pharyngitis, laryngitis, and atypical pneumonia in young adults.
coxsackievirus_b: Microbiology - Enterovirus causing epidemic pleurodynia (Bornholm disease) with acute intercostal muscle pain and pleuritis.
influenza_virus_drift: Microbiology - Minor point mutations in hemagglutinin or neuraminidase genes causing seasonal epidemics.
influenza_virus_shift: Microbiology - Major genetic reassortment of segmented RNA genome between human and animal strains causing global pandemics.
formoterol: Pharmacology - Long-acting $\\beta_2$-agonist with rapid onset of action; used for baseline asthma and maintenance COPD treatment.
budesonide: Pharmacology - Inhaled glucocorticoid reducing airway mucosal inflammation, microvascular hyperpermeability, and hyperresponsiveness.
beclomethasone: Pharmacology - Prodrug corticosteroid cleaved in bronchial mucosa to active metabolite; reduces eosinophilic airway inflammation.
benralizumab: Pharmacology - Monoclonal antibody targeting IL-5 receptor alpha ($IL-5R\\alpha$); induces direct NK-cell mediated apoptosis of eosinophils in severe eosinophilic asthma.
mepolizumab: Pharmacology - Humanized monoclonal antibody binding interleukin-5 (IL-5), preventing eosinophil recruitment and activation in asthma.
renal_cortex_medulla_junction: Anatomy - Boundary zone containing arcuate arteries and veins running parallel to the base of medullary pyramids.
juxtamedullary_nephron: Anatomy/Physiology - Nephron subclass with deep medullary Loops of Henle and vasa recta, crucial for generating hyperosmotic urine.
macula_densa_signaling: Physiology - Sodium chloride influx via NKCC2 stimulates adenosine release to constrict afferent arterioles when luminal $NaCl$ is high.
glomerular_filtration_barrier: A three-layered ultrafiltration structure comprising fenestrated capillary endothelium, the glomerular basement membrane (rich in heparan sulfate), and podocyte visceral epithelium with filtration slits bridged by nephrin.
renin_secretion: Physiology - Enzymatic release by juxtaglomerular cells triggered by renal hypoperfusion, sympathetic stimulation ($\\beta_1$), or low $NaCl$ at macula densa.
angiotensinogen: Physiology - Hepatocyte-derived alpha-2 globulin cleaved by circulating renin to produce inert Angiotensin I.
angiotensin_converting_enzyme: Physiology - Endothelial enzyme (primarily pulmonary) converting Angiotensin I to vasoactive Angiotensin II and inactivating bradykinin.
aldosterone_action: Physiology - Steroid hormone acting on principal cells to increase apical ENaC channels and $Na^+/K^+$-ATPase pumps, promoting $Na^+$ reabsorption and $K^+$ excretion.
atrial_natriuretic_peptide: Physiology - Cardiac hormone released upon atrial stretch; dilates afferent arteriole and constricts efferent arteriole to elevate GFR and natriuresis.
nephrotic_syndrome_minimal_change: Pathology - Most common cause of pediatric nephrotic syndrome; effacement of podocyte foot processes on EM; responds to corticosteroids.
membranous_nephropathy: Pathology - Common cause of adult nephrotic syndrome; subepithelial 'spike and dome' immune deposits; associated with anti-PLA2R antibodies.
diabetic_nodular_glomerulosclerosis: Pathology - Expansion of mesangium forming eosinophilic PAS-positive Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules; hallmark of advanced diabetic kidney disease.
post_streptococcal_glomerulonephritis: Pathology - Nephritic syndrome occurring 2-4 weeks after S. pyogenes infection; subepithelial 'humps' of IgG/C3 and starry-sky immunofluorescence.
crescentic_glomerulonephritis: Pathology - Histologic marker of severe rapid glomerular injury featuring fibrin, macrophages, and parietal cell proliferation in Bowman's space.
acute_tubular_necrosis: Pathology - Ischemic or toxic (aminoglycosides, radiocontrast) injury to renal tubular cells; muddy brown granular casts in urine.
pyelonephritis_acute: Pathology/Microbiology - Neutrophilic inflammation of renal parenchyma and pelvis caused by ascending UTI; WBC casts present in urine.
pyelonephritis_chronic: Pathology - Recurrent kidney infections leading to blunted calyces and corticomedullary scarring with thyroidization of renal tubules.
proteus_mirabilis: Microbiology - Urease-positive Gram-negative rod exhibiting swarming motility; hydrolyzes urea to ammonia, elevating urinary pH and forming struvite stones.
escherichia_coli_uti: Microbiology - Uropathogenic strains possessing P-fimbriae (pili) that adhere to uroepithelium; primary cause of uncomplicated UTIs.
furosemide: Pharmacology - Loop diuretic inhibiting $Na^+/K^+/2Cl^-$ cotransporter in thick ascending limb; increases renal calcium excretion.
hydrochlorothiazide: Pharmacology - Thiazide diuretic inhibiting $Na^+/Cl^-$ cotransporter in early DCT; increases calcium reabsorption and lowers urinary excretion.
spironolactone: Pharmacology - Non-selective aldosterone receptor antagonist inhibiting principal cell ENaC expression; causes gynecomastia and hyperkalemia.
acetazolamide: Pharmacology - Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor acting on PCT to block $HCO_3^-$ reabsorption; induces metabolic acidosis and alkalinizes urine.
lisinopril: Pharmacology - Long-acting ACE inhibitor used for hypertension and heart failure; reduces efferent arteriolar resistance to preserve renal function in early CKD.
valsartan: Pharmacology - Angiotensin II receptor blocker ($AT_1$ selective) providing renal protection without inhibiting bradykinin breakdown.
optic_chiasm: Anatomy - X-shaped midline structure where decussation of nasal retinal fibers occurs; pituitary adenoma compression causes bitemporal hemianopsia.
foramen_lacerum: Anatomy - Cartilage-filled base-of-skull opening; internal carotid artery passes horizontally across its superior aspect rather than directly through it.
trochlear_nucleus: Anatomy - Midbrain motor nucleus located at the level of the inferior colliculus giving origin to CN IV fibers.
subthalamic_fasciculus: Anatomy - Reciprocal fiber pathway connecting the subthalamic nucleus with the globus pallidus.
astrocyte_foot_processes: Histology - Perivascular end-feet of astrocytes covering cerebral capillaries to maintain blood-brain barrier integrity and regulate ion homeostasis.
ependymal_cells: Histology - Simple ciliated columnar epithelial cells lining cerebral ventricles and central canal of spinal cord, aiding CSF circulation.
microglia: Histology - Resident CNS macrophages derived from embryonic yolk sac mesoderm; transform into rod cells or gitter cells during parenchymal damage.
oligodendrocyte: Histology - Glial cell responsible for myelinating multiple CNS axons (up to 50 axons per cell); damaged in multiple sclerosis.
parkinson_disease: Pathology - Loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta; histologically identified by intracellular Lewy bodies containing alpha-synuclein.
alzheimer_disease: Pathology - Neurodegenerative disease showing extracellular amyloid-beta plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles composed of hyperphosphorylated tau.
creutzfeldt_jakob_disease: A rapidly progressive, fatal neurodegenerative prion disease characterized by spongiform vacuolation of gray matter, rapid cognitive decline, myoclonus, and 14-3-3 protein positivity in the CSF.
central_neurocytoma: Pathology - Benign intraventricular neuronal tumor in young adults arising near the septum pellucidum; uniform cells with perinuclear halos.
rabies_virus: Microbiology - Bullet-shaped (-)ssRNA rhabdovirus traveling retrogradely via dynein to CNS; produces Negri bodies in Purkinje cells and pyramidal neurons.
poliovirus_pathogenesis: Microbiology - Enterovirus invading Peyer patches before hematogenous spread to anterior horn motor neurons, inducing lower motor neuron flaccid paralysis.
borrelia_burgdorferi_cns: Microbiology - Spirochete transmitted by Ixodes tick causing neuroborreliosis (Lyme disease) marked by bilateral facial nerve palsy and lymphocytic meningitis.
naegleria_fowleri: Microbiology - Free-living amoeba penetrating cribriform plate from warm fresh water; causes rapidly fatal primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM).
donepezil: Pharmacology - Centrally acting reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used to improve cognitive performance in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
memantine: Pharmacology - Low-affinity uncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist protecting central neurons from glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity in Alzheimer's disease.
entacapone: Pharmacology - Peripheral catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) inhibitor preventing peripheral degradation of levodopa, enhancing CNS entry.
selegiline: Pharmacology - Selective irreversible Monoamine Oxidase B (MAO-B) inhibitor blocking central dopamine breakdown; used in Parkinson's disease.
pramipexole: Pharmacology - Non-ergot dopamine receptor agonist directly stimulating D2 and D3 receptors; used to delay levodopa initiation.
modafinil: Pharmacology - Non-amphetamine wakefulness-promoting agent used for narcolepsy; acts via complex elevation of hypothalamic dopamine and histamine.
horizontal_fissure_lung: Anatomy - Structural fissure present in the right lung separating the superior lobe from the middle lobe at the 4th costal cartilage level.
oblique_fissure_lung: Anatomy - Major lung fissure present bilaterally separating inferior lobes from superior (and middle) lobes; follows course of 6th rib.
lingula: Anatomy - Tongue-shaped projection of the left upper lung lobe homologous to the right middle lobe, adjacent to the cardiac notch.
costodiaphragmatic_recess: Anatomy - Potential pleural space at the inferior margin of pleural cavity; site of fluid collection during pleural effusion.
respiratory_bronchiole: Histology - Transition zone airway lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with scattered alveoli in walls, initiating the respiratory zone.
alveolar_pore_of_kohn: Histology - Interalveolar opening allowing collateral air movement between adjacent alveoli and equalization of intra-alveolar pressure.
bronchial_smooth_muscle: Histology - Spiral smooth muscle layer in bronchial walls regulating airway caliber; responsive to parasympathetic contraction and sympathetic relaxation.
serous_demilune: Histology - Crescent-shaped serous cell cap overlying mucous acini in mixed respiratory glands, secreting lysozyme and antimicrobial peptides.
alveolar_ventilation_rate: Physiology - Volume of fresh air reaching gas-exchange regions per minute ($VA = (VT - VD) \\times RR$).
transpulmonary_pressure: Physiology - Difference between alveolar pressure and intrapleural pressure ($P_{tp} = P_{alv} - P_{ip}$); maintains lung inflation.
work_of_breathing: Physiology - Energy expended to overcome elastic recoil of lungs/chest wall and non-elastic airway resistance during respiration.
diffusing_capacity_dlco: Physiology - Clinical measurement of carbon monoxide uptake to evaluate functional integrity of alveolar-capillary membrane.
idiopathic_pulmonary_arterial_hypertensi: A progressive vascular disorder characterized by vascular remodeling, plexiform lesions, and sustained elevation of mean pulmonary artery pressure (>20 mmHg at rest), leading to right ventricular failure (cor pulmonale).
squamous_cell_carcinoma_lung: Pathology - Central lung tumor strongly linked to smoking; characterized by keratin pearls, intercellular bridges, and hypercalcemia ($PTHrP$).
small_cell_lung_carcinoma: Pathology - Highly malignant central neuroendocrine lung tumor; exhibits salt-and-pepper chromatin, ACTH/SIADH paraneoplastic syndromes, and L-myc amplification.
adenocarcinoma_lung: Pathology - Most common primary lung cancer in non-smokers and females; peripheral location, TTF-1 positive, forms glandular/mucin structures.
streptococcus_pneumoniae_rsp: Microbiology - Encapsulated alpha-hemolytic Gram-positive diplococcus; bile soluble and optochin sensitive; major cause of lobar pneumonia.
mycoplasma_pneumoniae_adhesion: Microbiology - P1 adhesin protein allowing attachment to respiratory ciliated epithelial cells, inhibiting mucociliary clearance.
chlamydia_psittaci: Microbiology - Obligate intracellular bacterium contracted from infected birds (parrots); presents with atypical pneumonia and severe headache.
parainfluenza_virus: Microbiology - Paramyxovirus causing acute laryngotracheobronchitis (croup) in infants; produces subglottic stenosis ('steeple sign' on X-ray).
ciclesonide: Pharmacology - Inhaled prodrug corticosteroid activated by esterases in lung epithelium; minimizes systemic side effects and oral candidiasis.
flunisolide: Pharmacology - Inhaled anti-inflammatory corticosteroid suppressing airway mucosal cytokine synthesis and inflammatory cell influx.
glycopyrrolate: Pharmacology - Anticholinergic agent blocking muscarinic receptors; used via inhalation to reduce bronchospasm in COPD.
revefenacin: Pharmacology - Once-daily long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) nebulized solution indicated for COPD maintenance.
aminophylline: Pharmacology - Water-soluble salt complex of theophylline used IV for severe acute bronchodilator-refractory asthma exacerbations.
pirfenidone: Pharmacology - Anti-fibrotic oral drug inhibiting TGF-beta production; used to slow progression of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
renal_column_of_bertin: Anatomy - Cortical tissue extensions projecting downward between adjacent renal pyramids into the renal medulla.
renal_sinus: Anatomy - Fat-filled cavity within the renal hilum accommodating major/minor calyces, renal pelvis, renal blood vessels, and nerves.
ureteric_constrictions: Anatomy - Three natural anatomical narrowings of the ureter: ureteropelvic junction, pelvic brim crossing, and ureterovesical junction.
peritubular_capillaries: Anatomy/Physiology - Low-pressure capillary bed arising from efferent arterioles of cortical nephrons, surrounding PCT and DCT for reabsorption.
parietal_layer_bowmans_capsule: Histology - Simple squamous epithelium forming the outer boundary of Bowman's space, continuous with PCT epithelium.
principal_cells: Histology/Physiology - Main cell type of late distal tubule and collecting duct; reabsorbs sodium via ENaC and secretes potassium via ROMK.
intercalated_cells_alpha: Histology/Physiology - Acid-secreting cells of collecting duct containing luminal $H^+$-ATPase and basolateral $HCO_3^-/Cl^-$ exchangers.
intercalated_cells_beta: Histology/Physiology - Bicarbonate-secreting cells of collecting duct containing luminal $HCO_3^-/Cl^-$ exchangers and basolateral $H^+$-ATPase.
glomerular_hydrostatic_pressure: Physiology - Major driving force favoring ultrafiltration ($P_{gc} \\approx 45-50\\text{ mmHg}$), regulated by afferent and efferent arteriolar tone.
bowman_space_hydrostatic_pressure: Physiology - Opposing force to glomerular filtration ($P_{bs} \\approx 15\\text{ mmHg}$); elevated in urinary tract obstruction.
oncotic_pressure_gradient_renal: Physiology - Opposing capillary oncotic pressure favoring fluid retention; increases along length of glomerular capillary as fluid is filtered.
renal_auto_regulation_range: Physiology - Range of mean arterial pressure (~80 to 180 mmHg) over which GFR and renal blood flow remain nearly constant.
acute_tubular_necrosis_toxic: Pathology - Necrosis of PCT tubular epithelium caused by nephrotoxins like aminoglycosides, cisplatin, ethylene glycol, or contrast dyes.
diffuse_proliferative_glomerulonephritis: Pathology - Severe lupus nephritis (Class IV); wire-looping of capillaries under light microscopy due to extensive subendothelial immune complex deposits.
renal_cell_carcinoma_clear_cell: Pathology - Most common renal malignancy; arises from PCT epithelium; loss of VHL gene on chromosome 3p; lipid and glycogen rich cytoplasm.
oncocytoma_renal: Pathology - Benign renal epithelial tumor arising from intercalated cells; mahogany-brown appearance with central stellate scar.
staphylococcus_epidermidis_renal: Microbiology - Coagulase-negative Gram-positive coccus forming biofilms on indwelling Foley urinary catheters.
enterobacter_cloacae: Microbiology - Gram-negative lactose-fermenting rod causing nosocomial complicated urinary tract infections.
candidal_cystitis: Microbiology/Pathology - Fungal urinary tract infection caused by *Candida albicans*; presenting with pseudohyphae in urine in diabetic or catheterized patients.
adenovirus_hemorrhagic_cystitis: Microbiology/Pathology - Viral infection causing self-limiting acute hemorrhagic cystitis in children, marked by sudden hematuria and dysuria.
metolazone: Pharmacology - Thiazide-like diuretic inhibiting $Na^+/Cl^-$ cotransporter in DCT; maintains efficacy even at low GFR ($<30\\text{ mL/min}$).
indapamide: Pharmacology - Lipid-soluble thiazide-like diuretic causing dual action: distal nephron sodium excretion and vascular smooth muscle dilation.
triamterene_hydrochlorothiazide: Pharmacology - Combination diuretic formulation balancing potassium retention and depletion while treating hypertension.
nifedipine_renal_effect: Pharmacology - Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker inducing selective afferent arteriolar vasodilation to modulate intrarenal hemodynamics.
aliskiren: Pharmacology - Direct renin inhibitor blocking conversion of angiotensinogen to Angiotensin I; used in hypertension.
sacubitril: Pharmacology - Neprilysin inhibitor preventing degradation of natriuretic peptides (ANP, BNP); combined with valsartan for heart failure treatment.
anterior_white_commissure: Anatomy - Axonal bundle crossing the spinal cord anterior to the central canal; decussation site of the spinothalamic tract carrying pain and temperature.
lateral_spinothalamic_tract: Anatomy/Physiology - Ascending pathway conveying pain and temperature sensation; decussates at the anterior white commissure spinal level.
dorsal_column_medial_lemniscus: Anatomy/Physiology - Ascending pathway transmitting fine touch, vibration, and conscious proprioception; decussates at internal arcuate fibers in medulla.
corticospinal_tract_decussation: Anatomy/Physiology - Crossing of ~85-90% of motor fibers at the pyramidal decussation in caudal medulla forming lateral corticospinal tract.
purkinje_cell_layer: Histology - Middle layer of cerebellar cortex containing large bottle-shaped inhibitory neurons releasing GABA onto deep cerebellar nuclei.
granular_layer_cerebellum: Histology - Innermost cerebellar cortex layer packed with tiny granule cells whose parallel fibers synapse on Purkinje cell dendrites.
molecular_layer_cerebellum: Histology - Outermost layer of cerebellar cortex containing stellate cells, basket cells, and dendritic arbors of Purkinje cells.
schwann_cell_node_of_ranvier: Histology - Gaps between myelin sheath segments produced by individual peripheral Schwann cells allowing saltatory nerve conduction.
alzheimer_type_2_astrocyte: Pathology - Modified astrocyte with enlarged, pale nucleus seen in hyperammonemic states such as hepatic encephalopathy.
pick_disease: Pathology - Frontotemporal dementia marked by localized frontal/temporal lobe atrophy and spherical tau-positive intracellular Pick bodies.
central_pontine_myelinosis_etiology: Pathology - Demyelination of the base of the pons associated with rapid overcorrection of severe chronic hyponatremia.
subdural_hygroma: Pathology - Accumulation of clear cerebrospinal fluid in the subdural space resulting from a tear in the arachnoid membrane.
herpes_zoster_ganglionitis: Microbiology/Pathology - Reactivation of dormant Varicella-Zoster Virus in dorsal root ganglia, presenting as painful dermatomal vesicular rash.
enterovirus_meningitis: Microbiology - Coxsackievirus and Echovirus species causing aseptic viral meningitis; CSF shows lymphocytic pleocytosis and normal glucose.
hsv_1_temporal_predilection: Microbiology/Pathology - Neurotropic property of HSV-1 to preferentially affect temporal lobes and orbitofrontal cortex, causing hemorrhagic necrosis.
clostridium_tetani_toxin_transport: Microbiology/Physiology - Retrograde axonal transport of tetanospasmin from peripheral nerve terminals to CNS Renshaw inhibitory interneurons.
valproate_teratogenicity: Pharmacology - Inhibition of folic acid pathways by valproic acid leading to neural tube defects such as spina bifida apex.
carbamazepine_autoinduction: Pharmacology - Hepatic CYP3A4 enzyme induction by carbamazepine causing self-accelerated clearance and shortened half-life over time.
oxcarbazepine: Pharmacology - Prodrug voltage-gated sodium channel blocker with lower risk of autoinduction and marrow suppression than carbamazepine.
rufinamide: Pharmacology - Triazole derivative antiepileptic prolonging sodium channel inactive state; approved for Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
felbamate: Pharmacology - Antiepileptic inhibiting NMDA receptors and modulating GABA-A receptors; limited by risks of aplastic anemia and hepatic failure.
vigabatrin: Pharmacology - Irreversible inhibitor of GABA transaminase (GABA-T) elevating CNS GABA concentrations; carries risk of permanent visual field loss.
bronchial_veins: Anatomy - Drainage network returning blood from proximal bronchial walls; deep bronchial veins drain into pulmonary veins creating physiologic shunt.
costomedial_recess: Anatomy - Pleural reflection space where costal pleura meets mediastinal pleura anteriorly.
sublaryngeal_airway: Anatomy - Subglottic region extending from lower surface of vocal cords down to inferior border of cricoid cartilage.
internal_laryngeal_nerve: Anatomy - Sensory branch of superior laryngeal nerve (CN X) supplying laryngeal mucosa superior to vocal folds; mediates cough reflex arc.
respiratory_epithelium: Histology - Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells lining the nasal cavity, trachea, and major bronchi.
bronchiolar_club_cell_protein: Histology/Physiology - Secretoglobin 1A1 (CC16) produced by club cells; anti-inflammatory marker decreased in chronic respiratory toxic exposure.
interalveolar_septum: Histology - Structural wall between adjacent alveoli containing capillary network, elastic fibers, collagen type III, and basement membrane.
alveolar_macrophage_siderophage: Histology/Pathology - Hemosiderin-laden alveolar macrophages resulting from phagocytosis of extravasated red blood cells in chronic pulmonary congestion.
pulmonary_vascular_resistance: Physiology - Opposition to blood flow through pulmonary circuit ($PVR = (MPAP - PCWP) / CO$); lowest at functional residual capacity.
alveolar_dead_space: Physiology - Volume of ventilated alveoli that are underperfused or unperfused, failing to participate in gas exchange.
lung_recoil_pressure: Physiology - Inward elastic force exerted by lung parenchyma at a given lung volume, balanced by outward chest wall expansion at FRC.
hypercapnic_respiratory_drive: The primary physiological mechanism regulating ventilation under normal conditions, driven by central chemoreceptors in the medulla reacting to changes in CSF arterial PCO2 and pH.
idiopathic_pulmonary_fibrosis_pathogenes: Pathology - Repetitive micro-injuries to alveolar epithelial cells with aberrant repair, TGF-beta hypersecretion, and fibroblastic foci formation.
desquamative_interstitial_pneumonia: Pathology - Smoking-related interstitial lung disease characterized by massive accumulation of intra-alveolar pigmented macrophages.
pulmonary_alveolar_proteinosis: Pathology - Impaired alveolar macrophage GM-CSF signaling leading to intra-alveolar accumulation of PAS-positive acellular surfactant lipoprotein material.
hypersensitivity_pneumonitis_granuloma: Pathology - Non-caseating poorly formed granulomas and interstitial lymphocytic infiltrate triggered by inhaled organic dusts.
chlamydia_trachomatis_pneumonia: Microbiology - Neonatal staccato cough pneumonia acquired during birth; associated with peripheral eosinophilia and conjunctivitis.
staphylococcus_aureus_post_viral_pneumon: Microbiology/Pathology - Secondary bacterial necrotizing pneumonia following influenza infection; forms multiple cavitary lung abscesses.
aspergillus_fumigatus_aspergilloma: Microbiology/Pathology - Fungus ball occupying preexisting lung cavities (e.g., from old TB) presenting with hemoptysis and radiographic air-crescent sign.
pneumocystis_jirovecii: Microbiology/Pathology - Opportunistic atypical fungus causing interstitial pneumonia in AIDS ($CD4 < 200$); silver stain shows cup-shaped cysts.
olodaterol: Pharmacology - Ultra-long-acting $\\beta_2$-adrenoceptor agonist (Ultra-LABA) formulated for once-daily maintenance therapy in COPD.
aclidinium: Pharmacology - Long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) with rapid hydrolysis in plasma, reducing systemic anticholinergic adverse effects.
mometasone_furoate: Pharmacology - High-potency inhaled corticosteroid with extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism, minimizing systemic bioavailability.
dornase_alfa: Pharmacology - Recombinant human deoxyribonuclease I (rhDNase) reducing sputum viscosity in cystic fibrosis by cleaving extracellular leukocyte DNA.
ivacaftor: Pharmacology - CFTR potentiator increasing chloride channel gating probability in patients carrying specific CFTR mutations like G551D.
lumacaftor: Pharmacology - CFTR corrector chaperone facilitating proper folding and cell-surface trafficking of F508del mutated CFTR protein.
interlobar_arteries_kidney: Anatomy - Branches of segmental renal arteries ascending through renal columns toward the corticomedullary junction.
arcuate_arteries_kidney: Anatomy - Vessels running arch-like over bases of renal pyramids at corticomedullary border, giving rise to interlobular arteries.
interlobular_arteries_kidney: Anatomy - Radial cortical arteries originating from arcuate arteries and supplying afferent arterioles to individual glomeruli.
renal_sympathetic_innervation: Anatomy/Physiology - Postganglionic sympathetic fibers (T10-L1) stimulating JG cell renin release ($\\beta_1$) and renal tubular $Na^+$ reabsorption ($\\alpha_1$).
nephrin_protein: Histology/Physiology - Transmembrane cell adhesion protein of podocyte slit diaphragm; mutations cause congenital nephrotic syndrome of the Finnish type.
podocin: Histology/Physiology - Hairpin-like stomatin family protein localizing to podocyte foot process base; essential for slit diaphragm integrity.
juxtaglomerular_cells: Histology/Physiology - Modified smooth muscle cells of afferent arteriole storing and secreting renin in response to hypotensive stimuli.
extraglomerular_lacis_cells: Histology - Continuous with intraglomerular mesangium; transmit signals between macula densa and afferent arteriole via gap junctions.
free_water_clearance: Physiology - Volume of solute-free water cleared by kidneys per unit time ($C_{H_2O} = V - C_{osm}$); negative during urine concentration.
fractional_excretion_of_urea: Physiology - Diagnostic parameter ($FE_{Urea}$) used to evaluate acute kidney injury when diuretics render $FENa$ unreliable; $<35\\%$ indicates prerenal state.
cortical_collecting_duct_potassium_secre: Physiology - Passive potassium movement across principal cell apical membrane via ROMK channels driven by lumen-negative electrical potential.
bicarbonate_reabsorption_pct: Physiology - Apical $Na^+/H^+$ exchanger (NHE3) secretes $H^+$ to combine with filtered $HCO_3^-$, forming $H_2CO_3$ converted by brush border carbonic anhydrase.
dense_deposit_disease_c3nf: Pathology - Autoantibody (C3 nephritic factor) stabilizing C3 convertase, leading to persistent alternative complement pathway activation and dense GBM deposits.
alport_syndrome_molecular: Pathology - Mutations in COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5 genes impairing type IV collagen triple helix assembly, causing basket-weave GBM.
diabetic_arteriolosclerosis: Pathology - Hyaline arteriolosclerosis affecting BOTH afferent and efferent arterioles (pathognomonic for diabetes mellitus).
pauci_immune_crescentic_gn: Pathology - Glomerulonephritis with minimal immune complex staining on immunofluorescence; associated with ANCA-associated vasculitides.
candidal_pyelonephritis: Microbiology/Pathology - Ascending fungal kidney infection forming renal fungal balls in collecting system of immunocompromised patients.
mycobacterium_tuberculosis_renal: Microbiology/Pathology - Hematogenous renal spread causing sterile pyuria, cortical caseating granulomas, and ureteral strictures.
leptospira_interrogans_renal: Microbiology/Pathology - Spirochete causing Weil disease; acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, jaundice, hemorrhage, and impaired renal function.
corynebacterium_urealyticum: Microbiology - Urease-positive opportunistic pathogen causing encrusted cystitis and struvite stone formation in hospitalized patients.
finrenone: Pharmacology - Non-steroidal selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist reducing renal inflammation and fibrosis progression in chronic kidney disease.
empagliflozin_renal_effect: Pharmacology - SGLT2 inhibitor reducing proximal glucose and sodium reabsorption, restoring tubuloglomerular feedback and lowering intraglomerular pressure.
dapagliflozin: Pharmacology - SGLT2 inhibitor promoting glucosuria and natriuresis; slows diabetic and non-diabetic chronic kidney disease progression.
patiromer: Pharmacology - Non-absorbed potassium-binding polymer acting in the gastrointestinal tract to increase fecal $K^+$ excretion in chronic kidney disease.
sodium_zirconium_cyclosilicate: Pharmacology - Inorganic non-absorbed cation exchanger selectively capturing potassium ions in GI lumen; used for acute and chronic hyperkalemia.
patisiran: Pharmacology - Small interfering RNA (siRNA) targeting transthyretin mRNA; reduces amyloid deposition in hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis.
stria_terminalis: Anatomy - Axonal pathway serving as the major efferent tract from the amygdaloid complex to the septal area and hypothalamus.
habenula: Anatomy/Physiology - Epithalamic structure integrating limbic forebrain signals with midbrain monoaminergic centers involved in disappointment and aversion response.
inferior_salivatory_nucleus: Anatomy - Parasympathetic motor nucleus in the medulla giving origin to preganglionic fibers of CN IX reaching the parotid gland via otic ganglion.
edinger_westphal_parasympathetic_pathway: Anatomy/Physiology - Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers traveling on CN III to ciliary ganglion, supplying sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscles.
renshaw_cells: Histology/Physiology - Glycinergic inhibitory interneurons in anterior horn of spinal cord providing recurrent inhibition to motor neurons.
schwann_cell_basal_lamina: Histology - Continuous basement membrane surrounding peripheral myelinated and unmyelinated axons, essential for nerve regeneration guidance.
clarke_column_cuneocerebellar_tract: Anatomy/Physiology - Pathways delivering uncrossed unconscious muscle spindle and Golgi tendon organ signals from upper body to cerebellum.
pituicytes: Histology - Glial support cells with vascular end-feet residing in neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary), supporting oxytocin and ADH nerve terminals.
dementia_with_lewy_bodies: Pathology - Progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder, parkinsonism, and alpha-synuclein inclusions in cortex.
progressive_supranuclear_palsy: Pathology - Tauopathy marked by vertical gaze palsy, postural instability with backward falls, hummingbird sign on midbrain MRI, and tufted astrocytes.
corticobasal_degeneration: Pathology - Asymmetric tauopathy presenting with alien limb phenomenon, cortical sensory loss, and apraxia with prominent ballooned neurons.
subacute_combined_degeneration: Pathology - Demyelination of posterior and lateral columns of spinal cord due to Vitamin B12 deficiency; presents with loss of vibration/position sense and spastic paraparesis.
enterovirus_d68: Microbiology - Picornavirus species linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) in children, causing asymmetric extremity weakness and anterior horn spinal lesions.
mumps_virus_cns: Microbiology - Paramyxovirus causing parotitis and aseptic meningitis or encephalitis with characteristic orchiditis and elevated CSF lymphocytes.
staphylococcus_aureus_brain_abscess: Microbiology/Pathology - Hematogenous or direct spread causing ring-enhancing central necrotizing brain abscesses; common post-trauma or with endocarditis.
trienterovirus_meningitis: Microbiology - Coxsackieviruses A and B causing self-limiting febrile aseptic meningitis with clear CSF and normal glucose levels.
brivaracetam: Pharmacology - High-affinity SV2A ligand antiepileptic providing targeted synaptic vesicle modulation with lower behavioral side-effect profile than levetiracetam.
cannabidiol_epilepsy: Pharmacology - Non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid approved as adjunctive therapy for Dravet syndrome and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
fenfluramine: Pharmacology - Serotonergic agent modulating $5-HT_{2}$ receptors; repurposed at low doses for severe refractory childhood epilepsies.
cenobamate: Pharmacology - Dual-action antiepileptic inhibiting sodium currents and acting as positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors in focal seizures.
ganaxolone: Pharmacology - Synthetic neurosteroid serving as positive allosteric modulator of synaptic and extrasynaptic GABA-A receptors in CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
perivascular_space_of_virchow_robin: Anatomy/Histology - Fluid-filled immunologically active spaces surrounding cerebral microvessels as they penetrate the brain parenchyma.
crista_galli: Anatomy - Superior median process of the ethmoid bone providing anterior attachment for the falx cerebri.
sphenopalatine_foramen: Anatomy - Opening connecting pterygopalatine fossa to nasal cavity, transmitting sphenopalatine artery and nasopalatine nerve.
internal_intercostal_muscles: Anatomy/Physiology - Intercostal muscle layer whose fibers run caudally and posteriorly; active during forced expiration.
external_intercostal_muscles: Anatomy/Physiology - Intercostal muscle layer whose fibers run caudally and anteriorly; elevates ribs during forced inspiration.
type_3_collagen_pulmonary: Histology - Reticular collagen fibers abundant in alveolar septa providing elastic recoil and structural framework in delicate respiratory tissues.
bronchial_gland_serous_cells: Histology - Epithelial cells in submucosa producing antimicrobial proteins (lysozyme, lactoferrin, secretory component of IgA).
alveolar_interstitial_fibroblast: Histology/Pathology - Resident mesenchymal cells synthesizing extracellular matrix components; hyperactive state drives pulmonary fibrosis.
bronchial_ciliated_cell_axoneme: Histology - Microtubule arrangement (9+2 dynein pattern) facilitating mucociliary escalator movement; defective in Kartagener syndrome.
airway_closing_capacity: Physiology - Volume of gas in lungs at which small conductive airways in lower pulmonary zones begin to collapse during expiration.
functional_residual_capacity: Physiology - Resting equilibrium volume remaining in lungs after normal passive expiration ($FRC = ERV + RV$).
intrapleural_pressure_gradient: Physiology - Baseline subatmospheric pressure gradient (more negative at apex than base due to gravity), determining regional ventilation differences.
pulmonary_capillary_transit_time: Physiology - Duration (~0.75 seconds at rest) spent by erythrocytes in alveolar gas-exchange capillaries; shortened during vigorous exercise.
pulmonary_langerhans_cell_histiocytosis: Pathology - Smoking-associated interstitial lung disease featuring eosinophils, CD1a/S100-positive Birbeck granule-containing Langerhans cells, and cysts.
lymphangioleiomyomatosis: Pathology - Cystic lung disease in young females of childbearing age; proliferation of smooth muscle-like cells carrying TSC2 mutations and statin/mTOR reactivity.
diffuse_idiopathic_pulmonary_neuroendocr: Pathology - Rare precursor lesion for bronchial carcinoid tumors featuring widespread small airway neuroendocrine cell aggregates.
bacterial_tracheitis: Pathology/Microbiology - Severe life-threatening exudative infection of upper airway wall, most commonly caused by *Staphylococcus aureus* following viral croup.
burkholderia_cepacia_complex: Microbiology - Opportunistic Gram-negative rod causing severe necrotizing pneumonia ('cepacia syndrome') and lung transplant contraindication in CF patients.
nocardia_asteroides_lung: Microbiology/Pathology - Weakly acid-fast branching filamentous Gram-positive bacterium causing cavitating pulmonary lesions in immunocompromised hosts.
rhinovirus_pathogenesis: Microbiology - Picornavirus binding ICAM-1 entry receptors on upper airway ciliated epithelium, triggering local inflammatory cytokine storm.
blastomyces_dermatitidis: Microbiology/Pathology - Dimorphic endemic fungus causing granulomatous lung lesions; presents as broad-based budding yeast on histology.
velmanase_alfa: Pharmacology - Recombinant human alpha-mannosidase enzyme replacement therapy used to alleviate non-neurological respiratory manifestations.
nintedanib: Pharmacology - Small-molecule intracellular tyrosine kinase inhibitor (VEGFR, FGFR, PDGFR) blocking pro-fibrotic signaling in IPF.
ecallantide: Pharmacology - Recombinant plasma kallikrein inhibitor approved for acute attacks of hereditary angioedema with upper airway swelling.
icatibant: Pharmacology - Synthetic competitive bradykinin $B_2$ receptor antagonist used to treat life-threatening attacks of hereditary angioedema.
tezepelumab: Pharmacology - Monoclonal antibody targeting thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP), suppressing upstream airway inflammation across multiple asthma phenotypes.
glomus_granules_carotid_body: Histology/Physiology - Neurosecretory vesicles inside glomus type I cells containing dopamine and ATP, released during hypoxemia to trigger CN IX impulse.
renal_fascia_gerota: Anatomy - Collagenous connective tissue layer enclosing the kidney, adrenal gland, and perinephric fat, separating them from paranephric fat.
renal_vein_entrapment_syndrome: Anatomy/Pathology - Nutcracker syndrome; compression of left renal vein between superior mesenteric artery and abdominal aorta, causing left flank pain and hematuria.
ureteric_bud_derivatives: Anatomy/Histology - Embryonic outgrowth of Wolffian duct giving rise to ureter, renal pelvis, major/minor calyces, and collecting ducts.
metanephric_blastema_derivatives: Anatomy/Histology - Embryonic mesenchyme differentiating into glomerulus, Bowman's capsule, PCT, Loop of Henle, and DCT.
medullary_interstitial_cells: Histology - Lipid-laden interstitial cells of inner medulla producing prostaglandins ($PGE_2$) and glycosaminoglycans.
proximal_convoluted_tubule_brush_border: Histology - Dense apical microvilli carpet containing transporters, carbonic anhydrase IV, and endocytic machinery for protein reabsorption.
renal_clearance_of_inulin: Physiology - Gold standard measurement of GFR ($GFR = C_{inulin}$); completely filtered, neither reabsorbed nor secreted by nephrons.
tubular_reabsorption_of_bicarbonate_thre: Physiology - Plasma bicarbonate concentration (~24-26 mEq/L) above which filtered $HCO_3^-$ exceeds PCT reabsorptive capacity, resulting in bicarbonaturia.
potassium_adaptation_renal: Physiology - Chronic enhancement of principal cell $K^+$ secretion capacity in response to persistent high dietary potassium intake.
pressure_natriuresis: Physiology - Intrinsic renal reflex where elevated systemic arterial pressure increases sodium and water excretion independent of lumbar neural input.
c3_glomerulopathy: Pathology - Glomerular injury driven by dysregulated alternative complement pathway; includes dense deposit disease and C3 glomerulonephritis.
fibronectin_glomerulopathy: Pathology - Rare autosomal dominant kidney disease marked by massive subendothelial and mesangial fibrillar deposits of fibronectin.
collapsing_glomerulonephritis: Pathology - Severe variant of FSGS featuring global collapse of glomerular capillaries and prominent podocyte hyperplasia; linked to HIV and APOL1 risk alleles.
light_chain_cast_nephropathy: Pathology - Myeloma kidney; free monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains precipitate with Tamm-Horsfall protein, forming obstructive fractured intratubular casts.
corynebacterium_urealyticum_pathogenesis: Microbiology/Pathology - Alkaline encrusted cystitis and pyelonephritis driven by intense urease activity precipitating struvite crystals in bladder walls.
schistosoma_haematobium_egg_morphology: Microbiology - Large oval eggs possessing a prominent terminal spine; diagnostic feature in urine sedimentation of infected patients.
leptospira_interrogans_transmission: Microbiology - Exposure to water contaminated with infected animal urine; enters via mucosal abrasions to cause renal tubulointerstitial failure.
vesicoureteral_reflux_microbiology: Pathology/Microbiology - Retrograde urine flow from bladder to kidneys during micturition due to incompetent ureterovesical valve; major risk for recurrent pyelonephritis.
sparcentan: Pharmacology - Dual endothelin $ET_A$ and angiotensin II $AT_1$ receptor antagonist approved to reduce proteinuria in primary IgA nephropathy.
pegvaliase: Pharmacology - PEGylated recombinant phenylalanine ammonia lyase reducing toxic metabolite accumulation impacting neuro-renal axes.
lumasiran: Pharmacology - Hydroxyacid oxidase 1 (HAO1)-directed siRNA decreasing glycolate oxidase levels, preventing oxalate production in Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1.
nedosiran: Pharmacology - Lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA)-directed siRNA targeting hepatic oxalate synthesis pathway for hyperoxaluria treatment.
vaptans_aquaretic_effect: Pharmacology - Selective vasopressin receptor blockade causing solute-free renal water excretion (aquired diabetes insipidus model) without electrolyte wasting.
satavaptan: Pharmacology - Selective oral vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist investigated for dilutional hyponatremia management.
juxtaglomerular_apparatus: A specialized regulatory structure composed of macula densa cells in the distal convoluted tubule, juxtaglomerular renin-secreting cells in the afferent arteriole, and extraglomerular mesangial cells.
proximal_convoluted_tubule_histology: Segment lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with an extensive apical brush border (microvilli) and abundant mitochondria, reabsorbing ~65% of filtered water, Na+, Cl-, HCO3-, and all glucose and amino acids.
loop_of_henle_countercurrent_multiplier: System established by the thick ascending limb (impermeable to water, active Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransport via NKCC2) that creates a hyperosmotic medullary gradient required for urine concentration.
distal_convoluted_tubule_physiology: Early segment responsible for reabsorbing Na+ and Cl- via the thiazide-sensitive NCCT cotransporter, impermeable to water, and regulated by parathyroid hormone for Ca2+ reabsorption.
collecting_duct_principal_cells: Cells mediated by aldosterone (upregulating ENaC channels and Na+/K+ ATPase) for Na+ reabsorption and K+ secretion, and by ADH (inserting Aquaporin-2 channels) for water reabsorption.
collecting_duct_intercalated_cells: Alpha-intercalated cells secrete H+ via H+-ATPase and H+/K+-ATPase to reabsorb HCO3- (acid excretion), while beta-intercalated cells secrete HCO3- and reabsorb H+ during alkalosis.
renal_clearance_and_gfr: The volume of plasma cleared of a substance per unit time; Inulin or creatinine clearance estimates GFR, while Para-aminohippuric acid (PAH) clearance measures renal plasma flow.
renin_angiotensin_aldosterone_system: Endocrine cascade triggered by renal hypoperfusion or low NaCl at macula densa; renin converts angiotensinogen to Ang I, ACE converts Ang I to Ang II (causing vasoconstriction and aldosterone release).
tubuloglomerular_feedback: Intrarenal reflex where increased NaCl delivery to the macula densa triggers adenosine release, causing afferent arteriolar constriction to normalize GFR.
minimal_change_disease_pathology: Most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children, characterized by normal glomeruli on light microscopy, absence of immune deposits, and effacement of podocyte foot processes on electron microscopy.
focal_segmental_glomerulosclerosis: Nephrotic syndrome characterized by segmental sclerosis in some glomeruli, commonly associated with HIV, heroin use, or obesity, showing hyalinosis and podocyte effacement.
membranous_nephropathy_pathology: Nephrotic syndrome in adults often linked to anti-PLA2R antibodies, showing subepithelial immune complex deposits creating a 'spike and dome' appearance on silver stain.
diabetic_nephropathy_pathology: Microvascular complication characterized by nodular glomerulosclerosis (Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules), mesangial expansion, and basement membrane thickening.
acute_poststreptococcal_glomerulonephrit: Nephritic syndrome occurring 1-3 weeks post-streptococcal infection, showing hypercellular glomeruli, subepithelial 'humps' of IgG/C3, and low serum C3 levels.
rapidly_progressive_glomerulonephritis: Severe nephritic syndrome featuring crescent formation in Bowman's space composed of proliferating parietal epithelial cells and monocytes; caused by Goodpasture, ANCA vasculitis, or immune complexes.
ig_a_nephropathy_berger_disease: Most common glomerulonephritis worldwide, presenting as episodic gross hematuria following upper respiratory infections; characterized by mesangial IgA immune complex deposition.
acute_tubular_necrosis_pathology: Intrinsic acute kidney injury caused by ischemia or nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, contrast), featuring tubular cell sloughing, muddy brown granular casts, and loss of concentrated urine capability.
acute_interstitial_nephritis: Drug-induced hypersensitivity reaction (NSAIDs, penicillins, PPIs) presenting with fever, rash, eosinophilia, oliguria, and WBC casts in urine.
polycystic_kidney_disease_autosomal_domi: Genetic disorder caused by PKD1 or PKD2 mutations, leading to bilateral renal cyst enlargement, flank pain, hypertension, hepatic cysts, and berry aneurysms.
loop_diuretics_furosemide: Potent diuretics that inhibit the NKCC2 cotransporter in the thick ascending limb, abolishing the medullary concentration gradient, increasing renal excretion of Na+, Cl-, K+, Ca2+, and Mg2+.
thiazide_diuretics_hydrochlorothiazide: Diuretics that inhibit the NCCT cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule, increasing Na+ and Cl- excretion while decreasing urinary Ca2+ excretion.
potassium_sparing_diuretics_spironolacto: Competitive antagonist of aldosterone receptors in principal cells, preventing ENaC and Na+/K+ ATPase synthesis, causing mild natriuresis and retention of K+ and H+.
ace_inhibitors_lisinopril: Drugs that block conversion of Ang I to Ang II, dilating efferent arterioles to decrease intraglomerular pressure and slow diabetic nephropathy progression, but can cause dry cough and hyperkalemia.
carbonic_anhydrase_inhibitors_acetazolam: Diuretics acting on the proximal convoluted tubule by inhibiting carbonic anhydrase, blocking HCO3- reabsorption and causing urinary alkalinization and metabolic acidosis.
escherichia_coli_pyelonephritis: Uropathogenic E. coli producing P fimbriae (pili) that adhere to urothelium, ascending to cause tubulointerstitial inflammation, neutrophil infiltrates, and WBC casts.
proteus_mirabilis_uti: Urease-producing gram-negative bacterium that hydrolyzes urea to ammonia, elevating urine pH and predisposing to magnesium ammonium phosphate (struvite) staghorn calculi.
blood_air_barrier_histology: The ultra-thin structural continuous barrier located in the alveoli consisting of capillary endothelial cells, fused basement membranes, and type I alveolar epithelial cells facilitating optimal O2 and CO2 diffusion.
pulmonary_circulation_physiology: A low-resistance, high-compliance vascular circuit receiving the entire cardiac output from the right ventricle, uniquely exhibiting hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction to divert blood flow away from poorly ventilated alveoli.
anatomic_dead_space: The volume of conducting airways (approximately 150 mL in healthy adults) extending from the nose/mouth down to the terminal bronchioles where no gas exchange occurs.
physiological_dead_space: The total volume of air inspired that does not participate in gas exchange, calculated via the Bohr equation and comprising anatomic dead space plus alveolar dead space.
hypoxic_respiratory_drive: A compensatory ventilatory drive monitored by peripheral chemoreceptors located in the carotid and aortic bodies, becoming the dominant driver of breathing when arterial PaO2 drops below 60 mmHg.
pneumothorax_pathology: Accumulation of air within the pleural cavity leading to lung collapse, classified into spontaneous (primary or secondary), traumatic, and life-threatening tension pneumothorax causing mediastinal shift.
bronchiectasis_pathology: Permanent, abnormal dilation of bronchi and bronchioles caused by chronic necrotizing airway inflammation and destruction of muscular/elastic tissue, typically presenting with massive foul-smelling purulent sputum.
sarcoidosis_pathology: A multisystem non-caseating granulomatous disorder of unknown etiology, commonly affecting young adults and presenting with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, pulmonary infiltrates, and elevated serum ACE levels.
legionella_pneumophila_micro: A fastidious gram-negative rod isolated on BCYE agar, transmitted via aerosols from contaminated air conditioning or water systems, causing severe lobar pneumonia with hyponatremia and neurological symptoms.
respiratory_syncytial_virus_micro: An enveloped negative-sense RNA virus featuring F proteins that cause cell fusion (syncytia), representing the major cause of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in infants.
pneumocystis_jirovecii_micro: An opportunistic fungal pathogen causing interstitial pneumonia in immunocompromised individuals (CD4 <200), diagnosed via silver stain showing cup-shaped cysts in bronchoalveolar lavage.
tiotropium_pharmacology: A long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) that competitively blocks M3 receptors in bronchial smooth muscle, used as a maintenance bronchodilator in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
caffeine_citrate_apnea_of_prematurity: A methylxanthine derivative that stimulates the central respiratory center in the medulla, increases diaphragm contractility, and blocks adenosine receptors to prevent apneic episodes in preterm infants.
glomerular_filtration_rate_autoregulatio: Intrinsically controlled mechanisms (myogenic response and tubuloglomerular feedback) maintaining a stable GFR over renal perfusion pressures ranging between 80 to 180 mmHg.
goodpasture_syndrome_pathology: An autoimmune disorder caused by anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibodies directed against the alpha-3 chain of collagen type IV, leading to rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage.
nephrogenic_diabetes_insipidus: Impaired renal response to circulating antidiuretic hormone (ADH) at the collecting duct, leading to polyuria, polydipsia, hypernatremia, and dilute urine.
nephrolithiasis_calcium_oxalate: The most common form of kidney stone, visible on radiography as radiopaque envelope-shaped crystals, associated with hypercalciuria, hyperoxaluria, and low urinary citrate.
vaptans_tolvaptan_pharmacology: Selective vasopressin V2 receptor antagonists that block ADH action in collecting ducts, promoting aquaresis (free water excretion) without electrolyte wasting in hyponatremia.
loop_diuretic_ototoxicity: A dosage-dependent adverse effect of loop diuretics (especially ethacrynic acid and high-dose furosemide) caused by alterations in endolymph electrolyte composition in the inner ear.
brain_abscess_pathology: A localized focal parenchymal infection containing purulent necrosis, often surrounded by a vascularized collagen capsule and vasogenic edema, originating from hematogenous spread or contiguous sinus/mastoid infections.
subdural_hematoma_pathology: Bleeding into the space between the dura mater and arachnoid membrane caused by rupture of delicate bridging veins, appearing as a crescent-shaped lesion crossing suture lines on CT.
epidural_hematoma_pathology: Bleeding into the space between the inner skull table and dura mater, almost always caused by traumatic rupture of the middle meningeal artery associated with temporal bone fractures (biconvex lesion).
subarachnoid_hemorrhage_pathology: Bleeding into the subarachnoid space, most commonly caused by rupture of a saccular (berry) aneurysm in the Circle of Willis, presenting with sudden onset 'thunderclap headache'.
myasthenia_gravis_pathology: An autoimmune neuromuscular disorder caused by autoantibodies directed against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (AChR) at the neuromuscular junction, presenting with fatigable ptosis, diplopia, and muscle weakness.
lambert_eaton_myasthenic_syndrome: A paraneoplastic autoimmune disorder associated with small cell lung cancer, caused by antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels, leading to muscle strength improvement upon repeated exertion.
pyridostigmine_pharmacology: A peripherally acting reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that prolongs the action of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, serving as first-line symptomatic treatment for myasthenia gravis.
mannitol_pharmacology: An osmotic diuretic that increases plasma osmolality, drawing water out of parenchymal tissue into the intravascular space, used to rapidly decrease intracranial and intraocular pressure.
wernicke_korsakoff_syndrome: A neuro-cognitive manifestation of thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency, classically observed in chronic alcoholism, featuring the triad of ataxia, ophthalmoplegia, and confusion (Wernicke), which can progress to irreversible anterograde amnesia and confabulation (Korsakoff).
syringomyelia_pathology: A cystic cavitation (syrinx) within the spinal cord central canal, often associated with Chiari I malformation, classically causing a sensory dissociation characterized by loss of pain and temperature sensation in a 'cape-like' distribution with preserved fine touch.
guillain_barre_syndrome: An acute post-infectious demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy, often triggered by Campylobacter jejuni gastroenteritis, leading to ascending muscle weakness, loss of deep tendon reflexes, and albuminocytologic dissociation in the CSF.
normotensive_hydrocephalus: A form of hydrocephalus characterized by impaired CSF reabsorption by arachnoid villi, presenting with the classic clinical triad of urinary incontinence, gait apraxia, and dementia ('wet, wobbly, and wacky') with normal opening pressure on lumbar puncture.
brown_sequard_syndrome: A spinal cord hemisection resulting in ipsilateral loss of motor function (corticospinal tract) and proprioception/vibration (dorsal column) at and below the lesion level, combined with contralateral loss of pain and temperature sensation (spinothalamic tract) starting 1-2 segments below.
carbidopa_pharmacology: A peripheral aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase inhibitor that does not cross the blood-brain barrier; co-administered with levodopa to prevent its peripheral breakdown into dopamine, increasing central CNS availability and reducing nausea.
sumatriptan_pharmacology: A 5-HT1B/1D serotonin receptor agonist causing intracranial vasoconstriction and inhibition of vasoactive neuropeptide release from trigeminal nerve terminals, used as acute abortive therapy for migraine attacks.
donepezil_pharmacology: A centrally acting reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that elevates synaptic acetylcholine concentrations in the brain, used to provide modest symptomatic benefit in Alzheimer's dementia.
pulmonary_artery_wedge_pressure: An indirect measure of left atrial pressure obtained via a Swan-Ganz pulmonary artery catheter, crucial for differentiating cardiogenic pulmonary edema (elevated PAWP) from non-cardiogenic edema/ARDS (normal PAWP).
cheyne_stokes_respiration: An abnormal breathing pattern characterized by alternating periods of crescendo-decrescendo hyperpnea followed by central apnea, commonly caused by advanced heart failure or bilateral stroke.
hypoxic_pulmonary_vasoconstriction: An intrinsic physiological reflex mechanism in pulmonary arterioles that constricts blood vessels supplying poorly ventilated alveoli, redirecting perfusion toward adequately ventilated lung regions to optimize V/Q matching.
alpha_1_antitrypsin_deficiency: An autosomal codominant genetic disorder resulting in misfolded protein accumulation in the liver (PAS-positive globules) and panacinar emphysema in the lungs due to uninhibited neutrophil elastase activity.
silicosis_pathology: An occupational pneumoconiosis resulting from inhalation of crystalline silica particles, histologically marked by fibrotic nodules in the upper lung zones and eggshell calcifications of hilar lymph nodes, increasing susceptibility to tuberculosis.
asbestosis_pathology: A diffuse interstitial fibrosing pneumoconiosis associated with asbestos exposure, featuring golden-brown dumbbell-shaped ferruginous bodies and pleural plaques, carrying high risk for lung carcinoma and malignant mesothelioma.
streptococcus_agalactiae_meningitis: A Group B beta-hemolytic gram-positive streptococcus (CAMP test positive) that colonizes the female genitourinary tract, representing the leading cause of neonatal sepsis and meningitis.
varenicline_pharmacology: A partial agonist at alpha-4-beta-2 neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors that reduces nicotine cravings while blunting the rewarding effects of smoking.
roflumilast_pharmacology: An oral phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE-4) inhibitor that increases intracellular cAMP levels in inflammatory cells, used to reduce severe exacerations in patients with chronic bronchitis and severe COPD.
effective_renal_plasma_flow: The volume of renal plasma delivered to functional nephrons per unit time, estimated clinically using the clearance of Para-Aminohippuric acid (PAH) due to its near-complete filtration and tubular secretion.
fanconi_syndrome_renal: A generalized absorptive defect in the proximal convoluted tubule leading to excessive urinary loss of glucose, amino acids, uric acid, phosphate, and bicarbonate, presenting with glucosuria with normal plasma glucose, hypophosphatemia, and proximal RTA.
